1.why: The system enforces server-side authorization on MFA endpoints by requiring a verified session owner (requireSession with requireIdentity=true).

2.why: The same verification code does not work for any other user; each session has a unique identityCode tied to the session.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated on logout (sessions.delete), but enabling MFA does not explicitly invalidate existing sessions.

4.why: OTP secrets and backup codes are stored encrypted (AES-GCM) or hashed (SHA-256) at rest.

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated using crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are not persisted in browser storage or non-HttpOnly cookies (only HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies are used).

7.why: Server-side input validation is performed (e.g., validEmail, validPhone, validOtp) before processing.

8.why: Output encoding is applied in the HTML template (e.g., nonce-based CSP, escaped dynamic content).

9.why: Redirects are not explicitly handled in the code, but the system does not allow open redirects (no dynamic redirect logic).

10.why: Secure response headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options) are set in baseHeaders.

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are not exposed in logs, URLs, or error output (generic error messages are used).

13.why: Verification codes (identityCode) are single-use (consumed flag) and time-bound (expiresAt).

14.why: Repeated failed verification attempts are rate-limited (identityFailures, otpFailures, recoveryFailures with lockout).

15.why: Session identifiers are rotated on authentication (new session ID on sign-in), but idle/absolute timeouts are enforced, and invalidation on logout is explicit.
